Subject: Redwood Marketplace options for annual commitment (intro)

Jonas —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Our procurement team asked me to get clarification on two things before we move to legal: how Redwood structures annual / multi-year prepay offers through cloud marketplaces (AWS in our case), and how the ramp schedule and billing cadence work for a 3-year commitment.

High level asks:
- Example payment profile across 3 years (what portion is prepaid vs invoiced/true-up)
- Discount tiers for 1yr vs 3yr prepay (and how those map to list vs marketplace SKU pricing)
- How credits/unused prepay are handled on termination or underuse
- Whether we can have net-60 terms for the non-prepaid portion

Can you send a short proposal and any templates you normally use for a marketplace private offer? We prefer to finalize commercial structure first so our procurement can draft the PO.

Thanks,

Linda Cho
Head of Procurement, Acme Corp
procurements@acme-corp.com

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Redwood Marketplace options for annual commitment (intro)

Linda — thanks, and great to meet last week. High-level proposal below — attaching a worked ramp spreadsheet and our private-offer terms for your procurement/legal team.

Option A — 12-month annual prepay (simple)
- Commitment: 1 year prepaid up-front
- Discount: 18% off list for annual prepaid SKU
- Billing: Redwood issues an invoice upon execution; customer pays directly (or can route via AWS Marketplace if preferred)
- Termination: No refund after execution (standard for prepaid SKUs)

Option B — 3-year ramped prepaid (recommended for unit-cost reduction)
- Commitment: 3-year total spend committed, invoiced as annual prepay at the start of each year
- Ramp cadence (example): Year 1 = 40% of total committed value, Year 2 = 30%, Year 3 = 30%
- Effective discount: 26% off list for 3-year prepay (reflects multi-year term and predictable capacity reservation)
- Billing cadence: annual invoices at each year anniversary; we can support annual prepay via AWS Marketplace private offer so payment flows through AWS, or Redwood can invoice directly if you prefer PO-based payment (net-60 available on invoiced components)
- Unused credit handling: credits are applied to future usage within the committed term; after term ends, unused prepaid balance is forfeited unless you elect a pro-rated refund in the private-offer SOW (we can offer a limited pro-rate on a 3-year term subject to an administrative fee)

Marketplace specifics and SKU mapping
- For AWS Private Offers we publish committed SKUs that map to the same API routes you use in-hosted mode; pricing on the private-offer must match the commitment tiers we agree with you and will be set per-annual-SKU.
- AWS billing vs Redwood invoicing: marketplace route gives consolidated billing through AWS (simpler for central procurement) but vendor payouts to Redwood take an AWS settlement lag (standard). Direct Redwood invoicing keeps settlement real-time but requires a PO. We can do either — we put the default in the attached terms.

Next steps
- I attached a ramp spreadsheet (Acme_Ramp_Proposal_v3.xlsx) with numbers for a $2.4M 3-year total example; please confirm if the Year1 % needs to change for cash-flow.
- If this looks good, we’ll prepare the AWS Private Offer draft and the SOW Annex A for signature.

Thanks — copying Marissa and Rishi to keep finance and deal ops aligned.

Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Director | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: RE: ACME - Marketplace annual commitment structure & billing cadence (internal)

Jonas — quick internal note on margin and approval thresholds.
- If we give 26% on a 3yr prepaid, finance flags the following: effective gross margin compression ~6 points vs 1yr prepay; need exec sign-off for discounts beyond 25% unless this is strategic (ACME is mid-enterprise but referenceable).
- Recommend we counter with a structured concession: 25% for 3yr if Year1 prepay >= 40% AND ACME signs a 12-month usage milestone (we'll add a milestone that unlocks an extra 1% credit at the start of Year 2).
- Also prefer to keep unused-credit refund as a pro-rate with 90-day admin (rather than a full forfeiture) for procurement sensitivity.

Putting draft language in the attached SOW-AnnexA.docx and calling out the milestone. If ACME pushes Year1 down to 25% we should adjust the 3yr discount to 22% to preserve economics.

Marissa
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

--
Attachment: note_margin_impact.pdf (internal)

Jonas / Marissa — thanks for the detailed options and the attachments. A couple of clarifications from procurement:

1) Cash flow constraint: Acme can only commit 25% of the 3-year total as Year1 prepay. Can you show the numbers for a 3yr cadence with Year1=25% / Year2=37.5% / Year3=37.5%? We need to see how that impacts the effective unit price / discount.

2) Net terms: we can accept annual prepay via AWS Marketplace, but for any invoiced or non-prepaid portion we need net-60. Please confirm Redwood can accept net-60 on the non-prepaid invoices.

3) Marketplace parity with Azure: we may evaluate an Azure deployment next year — does the private-offer pricing structure carry across cloud marketplaces or will we need separate SKUs/offers?

4) One concession request: can you include a 90-day pro-rated refund clause on unused prepaid balance if ACME terminates for convenience after Year 1 (subject to admin fee)? Procurement prefers that to full forfeiture.

Thanks — once we receive the adjusted spreadsheet we can route to legal for a private-offer review and PO generation.

Linda

Subject: Re: ACME - Marketplace annual commitment structure & billing cadence (final)

Linda — appreciate the clarity. Updated proposal attached and answers below.

1) Ramp with Year1=25%: attached spreadsheet now shows year-by-year invoice amounts for a $2.4M 3-year total with Year1=25% / Year2=37.5% / Year3=37.5%. Under that cadence the effective overall discount we can offer is 23% (we’re stepping the discount down because Year1 prepay reduces our early-term cash and capacity guarantee). I included a small sensitivity tab so you can see the unit price delta if Year1 moves between 20-45%.

2) Net-60: Redwood can accept net-60 on any invoiced portion (non-prepaid). For AWS Marketplace prepay routed via AWS, payments follow AWS settlement cadence — if you prefer the net-60 guarantee on a Redwood invoice we recommend doing Redwood invoicing for the non-prepaid years and using AWS private-offer only for the prepaid SKU. We call that a split-billing flow; attached terms include language for both options.

3) Marketplace parity: private offers are per-cloud SKU. We can mirror pricing and discount structure across AWS and Azure, but each cloud requires its own private-offer and SKU mapping. We can commit to parity language in the SOW (i.e., same effective unit price on Azure private-offer SKUs) but the contract will reference separate offers.

4) 90-day pro-rated refund: agreed — we can include a 90-day pro-rated refund for termination for convenience after Year 1, subject to a 3% admin fee and settling via Redwood invoice. This will be added to Annex A.

Next steps:
- I attached the updated Acme_Ramp_Proposal_v3.xlsx and SOW-AnnexA.docx with the 23% discount row, the payment-flow options, and the pro-rate language.
- If acceptable, please confirm and we will: 1) generate the AWS Private Offer draft; 2) create the DocuSign for Annex A and the order form; 3) align on PO and billing flow.

If you want a short call to walk procurement/legal through the private-offer flow (AWS vs direct invoicing), happy to set 30 mins next week.

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
